text:
jessica: Heads-up — customer AcmePayments reporting their Embeddings usage chart shows ~3x the expected units since yesterday. They say their app didn't change. Screenshot: https://acme.screenshots/abc123 :eyes:
acme-sre: Confirming on our side — we see the spike in the console under Org 789. Looks like 'embedding_units' jumped from ~12k/day to ~36k/day starting 2026-03-15 03:10 UTC. No new traffic from our end.
sam: Can you paste a sample request id from the time window? need to trace through ingress and the metering pipeline.
acme-sre: request_id: req_0a7f3c4e, model: text-embed-3-large, payload vector_count=1, tokens=42. We also have req_0a7f3d22 from same minute.
jessica: Customer attached the curl they used for bulk upserts: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." -d '{"input": ["doc1","doc2"], "model":"text-embed-3-large"}'``` They claim their SDK split vectors correctly (1 per input).
diego: I pulled logs for req_0a7f3c4e and see two downstream metering events emitted: meter_event(id=m_9b1, window=60s) and meter_event(id=m_9b2, window=1s) with identical counts. Looks like both raw_per_request and aggregated_per_window are being counted into the same metric.
alex: That's suspicious — a recent change in the metrics aggregator added a secondary emission for short TTL windows to support streaming dashboards. If the dashboard's queries sum both dimensions we could double/triple count.
morgan: Billing question: Are we charging customers off the summed chart? Customer is worried we'll bill them for the inflated number. We should check billing pipeline separation.
sam: Immediate triage: 1) stop using the dashboard's summed metric for billing decisions 2) set a short-lived alert to detect >2x overnight changes and pause auto-charge 3) create a rollback for the aggregator change if repro confirmed.
diego: Repro steps I used (can be shared): 1) run 100 single-input embedding requests at t0 2) watch /metrics/embeddings_per_min and /metrics/embeddings_short_window 3) query console chart that sums `embedding_units_total` over 1h -> saw 3x compared to raw vector_count. I can attach queries.
jessica: Customer asked for immediate credits/adjustment while you investigate. Acme is unhappy and opened a ticket (TKT-12902). Can Billing give a provisional refund?
morgan: I'll mark the account for manual review and provisionally apply a credit equal to the excess units (we'll finalize after root cause). Please add the exact time range and numbers.
acme-sre: Time range: 2026-03-15 03:10 -> 2026-03-16 06:00 UTC. Chart shows 104,321 units, our expected is ~34,700.
alex: Patch idea: change the dashboard query to dedupe by emission_tag before summing, and revert the short-window emitter in the aggregator for now. Sam/Diego, can you confirm that change won't drop legit metrics?
sam: I ran a canary in staging that disabled short-window emission and dashboards matched the raw counters. No loss of fidelity for the customer's usage patterns in our sampling.
diego: I'll push a dashboard fix: change query from `sum(embedding_units_total)` to `sum by(emission_tag)(embedding_units_total)` then `sum without(emission_tag)` after dedupe — essentially ignore duplicate tags. Will do rollback deploy in 10m.
deploy-bot: deploy started: rollout id r-2026-0315-agg-fix to console-service (3/3 hosts)
jessica: Provided Acme the temporary credit & ETA for fix. They appreciate quick response but want postmortem.
morgan: Note for billing: ledger entry created CHG-4551 provisional credit 69,621 units.
alex: Follow-ups: - Diego to confirm dashboard patch merged - Sam to open PR reverting emitter (or adding dedupe at source) - Postmortem + customer-facing writeup by EOD tomorrow.
diego: Dashboard patch merged and live. Early validation: chart for Acme now shows ~34.8k units for that range.
sam: Revert PR opened: revert/short-window-emitter. Queue for review.
jessica: I'll draft the customer note and include repro steps, root cause (duplicate emissions from aggregator + dashboard query summing), and remediation.
acme-sre: Thanks team, dashboard now matches our internal logs. We'll keep monitoring. :thumbsup:
